chief_complaint: BMI 14.8, restricts calories to 500 daily, cold intolerance and bradycardia
hpi_details: A 62-year-old female presents to the clinic with bmi 14.8, restricts calories to 500 daily, cold intolerance and bradycardia. She says the food restriction began about a year ago after a bereavement and has tightened steadily since, with progressive weight loss and generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks her body became hypersensitive after her bereavement and that strictly limiting food is necessary to keep her digestion clean and disciplined.
concerns: She is terrified of being forced to eat high-calorie meals that will make her gain weight and lose control of her body.
expectations: She hopes to receive vitamins or a metabolic supplement to warm her up and boost her energy without being told to eat more food.

investigation_events.title: Urgent eating-disorder medical-stability results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent medical-stability results are now available and support monitored admission; nutritional treatment should follow a supervised refeeding protocol.

results.value: Sinus bradycardia at 46 bpm with QTc 468 ms

clinical_knowledge.topic: Anorexia Nervosa restrictive evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Anorexia Nervosa restrictive is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Anorexia Nervosa restrictive: Medical hospitalization if unstable, careful refeeding, therapy, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: BMI 14.8, restricts calories to 500 daily, cold intolerance and bradycardia

A 62-year-old female presents to the clinic with bmi 14.8, restricts calories to 500 daily, cold intolerance and bradycardia. She says the food restriction began about a year ago after a bereavement and has tightened steadily since, with progressive weight loss and generalized fatigue.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Anorexia Nervosa restrictive.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Anorexia Nervosa restrictive.
reference_soap.plan: Urgently assess vital signs, ECG, electrolytes, glucose, hydration, and suicide risk. Given the very low BMI and severe restriction, arrange same-day specialist medical evaluation to determine need for monitored admission and supervised nutritional rehabilitation; do not initiate unsupervised refeeding.

must_ask.say: How do you feel about your body and your current weight?
What have you been eating in a typical day recently?
Do you exercise excessively, make yourself vomit, or use laxatives?
Have you noticed dizziness, fainting, or your heart racing or feeling irregular?
Have you had any fractures or noticed a loss of strength or energy?

history.answer: I have lost a dangerous amount of weight over the past year, and I feel freezing cold and weak all the time.
I have lost about 21 kilograms over the past twelve months, going from 60 kilos down to 39 kilos, and all my clothes hang loosely on me.
Yes, I strictly cut down my eating on purpose after my husband passed away a year ago, and I have kept tightening it since.
I strictly limit myself to around 500 calories a day, mostly having black coffee, clear vegetable broth, and plain lettuce leaves.
I'm terrified that people will try to force me to eat heavy food and make me gain weight.
history.topic: Body image and fear of weight

history.answer: I used to feel hungry, but now I ignore the hunger pangs and feel anxious if I eat anything outside my routine.
No, I have never forced myself to vomit, and I do not take laxatives or water pills.
I push myself to pace and walk for two to three hours every day to burn off calories, even when I feel faint.
No, I do not have any trouble swallowing or pain when swallowing.
I do not have heartburn or stomach pain, but I feel full almost immediately after taking just two bites.
I am very constipated and pass hard pellets only once every five or six days, but there has never been any blood or black tarry stool.
No, I do not have diarrhea, loose stools, or greasy foul-smelling stools.
I feel freezing cold constantly and have to wear multiple sweaters indoors, and I often feel dizzy when I stand up.
No, my heart feels like it beats very slowly, not fast or pounding, and I cannot stand heat at all.
No, I am not excessively thirsty, and I do not urinate unusually often.
No, I have not had any fevers, chills, or drenching night sweats.
No, I do not have any cough, phlegm, or coughing up blood.
No, I have not felt any swollen glands or lumps in my neck, armpits, or groin.
I felt profound grief after my husband died last year, and controlling my food became the only way I felt in control, but I have no wish to harm myself.
I wake up very early every morning and cannot get back to sleep because I keep thinking about food numbers.
My arms and legs feel so weak that climbing a flight of stairs takes all my energy, though I have not had any broken bones or falls.
I live by myself and can afford food, but I avoid keeping food in the house and prefer eating alone.
I had a routine checkup three years ago, including a normal stomach endoscopy, normal colonoscopy, and normal mammogram.
No, I have never had tuberculosis and have not been around anyone sick with it.
Ever since my loss, my stomach just can't tolerate heavy meals, so I feel I have to keep my food intake extremely clean and minimal.
I'm terrified that people will try to force me to eat heavy food and make me gain weight.
I was hoping you could give me a tonic or some vitamins to fix the constant chills and tiredness without making me change the way I eat.
I have never had high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid disease, or any chronic illness.
I have never had any operations or stayed overnight in a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medicines, over-the-counter pills, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to any medicines or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes, and I only have a small sip of wine on very rare social occasions.
I am retired from clerical work and live alone since my husband passed away last year.
There is no family history of eating disorders, thyroid disorders, or cancer.

exam.finding: Severely emaciated elderly female with marked temporal wasting and sunken eyes, dressed in multiple heavy sweaters.
Blood pressure 88/56 mmHg, pulse 46 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 35.8 °C, SpO2 98% on room air, BMI 14.8 kg/m².
Pale palpebral conjunctivae bilaterally; anicteric sclerae.
Dry oral mucous membranes, normal dentition without enamel erosion, and no oral ulcers.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth without palpable nodules.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without crackles or wheezes.
Marked sinus bradycardia with regular rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Scaphoid abdomen, soft, non-tender throughout, with no palpable masses or organomegaly.
Dry, flaky skin with fine lanugo-like hair on the forearms and back; no calluses on the knuckles or petechiae.
No pretibial or ankle edema bilaterally; prominent bony landmarks.
No resting, postural, or action tremor in the outstretched hands.
